findings.evidence: grep `pauliMatrix (Sum.inr`: SU2Generators.lean:61 `(1 / 2 : ℂ) * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr a) i j`; SpinDensityMatrix.lean:394 `(1 / 2 : ℂ) • PauliMatrix.pauliMatrix (Sum.inr k)`. SU2Generators.lean:103 docstring: "The fundamental `su(2)` Casimir: `Σₐ (σᵃ/2)(σᵃ/2) = (3/4) · 1`".
findings.fix: Keep one definition. Put the matrix-valued `spinHalf` in a module both consumers can import, delete `su2GenEntry`, set `genEntry := fun a i j => spinHalf a i j` in `su2NormalizedData`, and prove `SU2FundamentalStatement` from `sum_spinHalf_mul_self` (`congrFun₂`/`Matrix.ext_iff` plus `Matrix.sum_apply`, `Matrix.mul_apply`, `Matrix.one_apply`) instead of the `fin_cases` bash at SU2Generators.lean:104.
findings.issue: `spinHalf k = (1/2 : ℂ) • PauliMatrix.pauliMatrix (Sum.inr k)` duplicates `EpsilonEridani.QFT.QCD.RepresentationColor.su2GenEntry a i j = (1/2 : ℂ) * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr a) i j` (EpsilonEridani/QFT/QCD/SU2Generators.lean:60), which is the same object up to currying (`Matrix.smul_apply` is rfl). Likewise `sum_spinHalf_mul_self` (line 397), `∑ k, spinHalf k * spinHalf k = (3/4 : ℂ) • 1`, duplicates `SU2FundamentalStatement`/`su2FundamentalStatement` (SU2Generators.lean:83-86, 104-109), the entrywise `∑ a ∑ k (σᵃ/2)ᵢₖ (σᵃ/2)ₖⱼ = (3/4) δᵢⱼ`. The repo now carries two σᵃ/2's and two proofs of the same Casimir.

findings.evidence: crossProductMatrix ω = !![0, -ω 2, ω 1; ω 2, 0, -ω 0; -ω 1, ω 0, 0]; at ω = (1,0,0) this is !![0,0,0;0,0,-1;0,1,0], and I • it is `spinOne 0 = !![0,0,0;0,0,-I;0,I,0]` (SpinDensityMatrix.lean:150); same check passes for k = 1 and k = 2.
findings.fix: Define `spinOne k := Complex.I • (Matrix.crossProductMatrix (Pi.single k 1)).map (↑)` (or at minimum add that identification as a lemma), and derive `spinOne_apply_swap`/`spinOne_apply_self` from `crossProductMatrix_transpose` via `Matrix.transpose_map` instead of case bashes. This also makes `crossProductMatrix_mulVec` (`[ω]ₓ *ᵥ v = ω ⨯₃ v`) available, which is the rotation-generator content the docstring at line 147 asserts.
findings.issue: `spinOne` hard-codes matrices that Physlib already has: `Matrix.crossProductMatrix` (upstream/Physlib/Physlib/Mathematics/Modules/CrossProductMatrix.lean:28), the 𝖘𝖔(3) hat map. Entry by entry, `spinOne k = Complex.I • ((Matrix.crossProductMatrix (Pi.single k 1)).map (↑· : ℝ → ℂ))` for k = 0,1,2. Consequently `spinOne_apply_swap` (line 162) restates `crossProductMatrix_transpose` (`(crossProductMatrix ω)ᵀ = -crossProductMatrix ω`, line 41) and `spinOne_apply_self` (line 167) is its diagonal case, each re-proved by a fresh `fin_cases` bash. EpsilonEridani also already tabulates the same ε symbol as `epsilon3` (EpsilonEridani/QFT/QCD/SU2Generators.lean:52).

summary: The new spin-one-half material re-defines σᵃ/2 and re-proves its 3/4 Casimir, both of which already exist in EpsilonEridani's SU2Generators.lean, and `spinOne` re-tabulates the 𝖘𝖔(3) hat matrices that Physlib already provides as `Matrix.crossProductMatrix`. The rest of the PR (polarizations, decomposition, positivity bounds, the RCLike PosSemidef bound) is new and reuses upstream API.
